Project 01 · Healthcare Operations

RecoupFinder

Local healthcare document search and matching

Problem

Finding specific recoupment information required manually searching large collections of EOB (Explanation of Benefits) and ERN (Electronic Remittance Notice) documents.

Solution

Built a local Python tool that extracts identifying information from a recoup report, searches the document library, matches likely records, and flags unresolved cases for human review.

Outcome

A repetitive manual process that could take hours became an almost immediate lookup while the source documents remained local.

Privacy-aware by design: local processing, no cloud connection, and human review for uncertain matches.
PythonLocal processingDocument matchingHuman review
Synthetic demonstration data only.
Project 02 · Product Building

GroceryCents

Shared meal planning, shopping, and savings platform

Problem

Meal planning, recipes, grocery lists, store promotions, and in-store shopping were fragmented across separate tools and manual steps.

Solution

Designed a mobile-first household application that connects weekly meal planning, saved recipes, shopping workflows, store organization, and relevant promotional savings.

Real-world iteration

The product is used by a real household, which means features have been refined through actual shopping trips, user feedback, pricing changes, integration failures, and retailer website changes.

A product is more than a feature list. The useful work is what happens after real people start using it.
Mobile-first designWorkflow automationExternal dataUser testing
Home → weekly planning → current store savings matched to the trip.
Project 03 · AI Systems

SCOTT.AI

Personal AI (Artificial Intelligence) operations platform

Problem

General-purpose AI conversations are useful, but recurring work, research, projects, learning, and decision-making can become fragmented across separate chats and tools.

Solution

Designed a mobile-first command center that organizes task-specific workflows, active projects, research, learning, and decision tools into one operating layer.

Example

Career Pathfinder captures practical constraints before comparing realistic career options, helping keep recommendations grounded in the user’s actual situation.

The focus is not “one chatbot that does everything.” It is focused workflows that give AI a useful place inside an ongoing system.

Project 04 · Workflow Discovery

Local Business Automation

Evidence-based opportunity discovery before implementation

Problem

“This company could use AI” is too vague to build or sell responsibly. A useful project needs a specific workflow problem and evidence that the gap is real.

Solution

Designed a system that researches local businesses, identifies potential workflow gaps, scores opportunities, checks for existing technology and conflicts, and separates public evidence from assumptions that still need owner validation.

Decision discipline

Promising findings move into deeper discovery before any implementation is proposed. The system explicitly warns when an assumption still needs to be confirmed.

Evidence first. A specific business problem, a realistic build, and a clear reason the change would matter.
Research workflowOpportunity scoringValidationSales enablement
Discover → review the evidence → validate the opportunity before proposing a build.
How I work

Business problem first.

I use a simple operating pattern that keeps experiments small, results testable, and the people doing the work involved in the decision.

1

Understand

Clarify the outcome, the current process, the people involved, and what is actually slowing the work down.

2

Build small

Create the smallest useful prototype or workflow that can test the idea without overcommitting.

3

Validate

Compare the result against the current process, check accuracy and edge cases, and keep human review where it matters.

4

Improve

Use feedback and measured results to decide whether the workflow should be refined, expanded, or discarded.
